batch_node.name: git-serious double-tap: tap repository page v0.1.0
batch_node.description: The instance's one hardcoded page (git-serious-double-tap#9): /double-tap/tap is git-serious's generic repository page (git-serious-tap#56, PR# 58, bundle 'git-serious repository page v0.1.0' at revision origin/feat/repository-page) copied with its own entity ids and every search scoped to the literal "unified-systems-com/tap" (open pull requests only) instead of the ?repo= / ?state= inputs. Same structure — identity, machinery, open pull requests, status wall, not-observed — so the two pages read alike today; the machinery scene is this page's own so the visualization can be teased out into something tap-specific without touching the product's generic scene. Nothing of git_serious's bundle is mutated; github_core's machinery projection is shared by USES_PROJECTION edge (an out-of-file endpoint).

node.name: tap
node.description: unified-systems-com/tap, the repository that builds TAP, on its own page: the generic repository page's structure (identity, machinery, open pull requests, the status wall for this repository, its not-observed workflows) with every search hardcoded to unified-systems-com/tap — the instance's privilege, not the product's (git-serious-double-tap#9). Takes no input; ?repo= and ?state= are ignored.

node.name: This repository · tap
node.description: Who this repository is, as the organization declares it: its role, criticality, lifecycle and owner are GitHub custom properties (github-core#77), read against the organization's own definitions — a dash is a declared property this repository has not set. The two 'read?' columns say whether the collector could read pull requests and properties at all: 'unobservable' means a blank below is a refusal, not an absence. (double-tap copy, scoped to unified-systems-com/tap.)

columns.title: Repository
columns.header_tooltip: owner/name. Opens the repository on GitHub.

columns.title: Role
columns.header_tooltip: The repository's one primary purpose, as the organization declares it: platform, plugin, product, support or fixtures.

columns.title: Criticality
columns.header_tooltip: Consequence of this repository failing or being compromised, for the organization as a whole — not current attention.

columns.title: Lifecycle
columns.header_tooltip: experimental, stand-up, active, maintenance, deprecated, draw-down or retired.

columns.title: Owner
columns.header_tooltip: The accountable owner: a team slug or a GitHub login (ownership-type says which).

columns.title: Default branch
columns.header_tooltip: The branch most controls default to targeting.

columns.title: Visibility
columns.header_tooltip: public, private or internal.

columns.title: PRs read?
columns.header_tooltip: observed = the collector read this repository's pull requests (zero below is then a fact); unobservable = it could not, so an empty list below means nothing; blank = never asked.

columns.title: Properties read?
columns.header_tooltip: observed = the organization's custom-property values were read (a dash is a declared property this repository has not set); unobservable = they could not be read; blank = never asked.

node.name: Machinery · tap
node.description: This repository's CI system as nested machinery (github_core's machinery projection, git-serious-tap#35): sources on the right, pipelines in the middle, outputs on the left; a job whose place cannot be resolved is drawn as unknown, never as known. The same projection the landing page draws with, over this page's own scene searches; scoped to unified-systems-com/tap. GitHub nodes open their html_url in a new tab. (double-tap copy, scoped to unified-systems-com/tap.)

entity.name: double-tap · tap — repository page: machinery scene nodes

node.name: double-tap · tap — repository page: machinery scene nodes
node.description: The machinery scene for the page's repository, one global WHERE scoped per variable: github.com (unfiltered, one), the repository's row, its workflows and declared jobs by full_name = $repo; environments, rulesets and apps unfiltered because their attachment is an edge and the layout module hides any no repository in the scene owns. The OWNING account is not matched here: since github-core#82 pull-request authors are github_account nodes too, so an unfiltered account match would float every author into the scene — the account rides the companion refs search, reached through OWNS_REPO. Refs ride there as well (they are git_core__git_ref with no full_name). Same picture as the landing page's scene, declared here so this page carries no default repository of its own. (double-tap copy: the literal unified-systems-com/tap replaces the $repo input; open pull requests only.)

query: WHERE r.data.full_name = "unified-systems-com/tap" AND w.data.full_name = "unified-systems-com/tap" AND j.data.full_name = "unified-systems-com/tap"

entity.name: double-tap · tap — open pull requests of a repository, most recently updated first

node.name: double-tap · tap — open pull requests of a repository, most recently updated first
node.description: The open pull requests against the page's repository (github_core__pull_request, github-core#82), most recently updated first. Envelope mode so the table receives the typed fields — the head commit's check rollup rides each row. The collected window is the thirty most recently updated pull requests per repository in any state; an open one older than that window is not here, and github_repository.pull_requests_total on the identity row is the honest count. (double-tap copy: the literal unified-systems-com/tap replaces the $repo input; open pull requests only.)

node.name: Open pull requests · tap
node.description: What is proposed against this repository right now, and where each proposal stands. Checks is GitHub's combined verdict on the pull request's head commit — every check run and commit status counted, App-produced ones included — and the count beside it is how many the verdict counted; a dash means nothing has run on that head, which is not green. Review and Mergeable are GitHub's own words: a first read of mergeability is often UNKNOWN, and that is what it says. The number opens the pull request on GitHub; the head branch opens it on the branch's own repository, which for a fork is not this one. Click anywhere else on a row for the pull request on the grid. (double-tap copy, scoped to unified-systems-com/tap.)

columns.title: PR
columns.header_tooltip: The pull request number. Opens it on GitHub.

columns.title: Title
columns.header_tooltip: The title as written.

columns.title: Author
columns.header_tooltip: Who opened it. A Bot author is an App.

columns.title: Head
columns.header_tooltip: The proposed branch. Opens it on the repository it lives in — a fork's branch opens on the fork.

columns.title: Base
columns.header_tooltip: The branch it asks to land on — the one whose rulesets gate the merge.

columns.title: Checks
columns.header_tooltip: GitHub's combined verdict on the head commit: SUCCESS, FAILURE, PENDING, ERROR or EXPECTED. A dash means no check has run on this head, which is not the same as green.

columns.title: n
columns.header_tooltip: How many check runs and commit statuses the verdict counted, App-produced ones included.

columns.title: Review
columns.header_tooltip: GitHub's review decision: APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, REVIEW_REQUIRED; blank when no review is required.

columns.title: Mergeable
columns.header_tooltip: GitHub's mergeability: MERGEABLE, CONFLICTING or UNKNOWN (computed lazily — a first read often says UNKNOWN).

columns.title: Updated
columns.header_tooltip: When GitHub last recorded a change on the pull request, in your local time. Hover for UTC.

Envelope mode for the table panel. Covers the collected window only. (double-tap copy: the literal unified-systems-com/tap replaces the $repo input; open pull requests only.)

node.name: Status wall — this repository · tap
node.description: Is anything broken here right now? The landing page's status wall, filtered to this repository: every collected run, newest first. The glyph is the trigger; the run number opens the run on GitHub; the branch opens the branch on GitHub. Elapsed, its ratio to the workflow's own baseline (▲ slower, ▼ faster, – not enough history) and the sample size (n) sort independently; a run still in flight shows a dash. History is the workflow's runs as a strip and opens the workflow page. Click anywhere else on a row for the run on the grid. (double-tap copy, scoped to unified-systems-com/tap.)

columns.header_tooltip: Trigger — what started the run: push, pull request, schedule, manual dispatch, a run chained off another run, or platform-originated (CodeQL, Copilot, Dependabot). Hover a glyph for its name.

columns.title: Run
columns.header_tooltip: GitHub's run number within the repository. Opens the run on GitHub.

columns.title: Branch
columns.header_tooltip: The branch or ref the run built. Opens the branch on GitHub.

columns.title: Conclusion
columns.header_tooltip: GitHub's terminal conclusion: success, failure, cancelled, skipped… A dash means the run has not concluded (queued or still running).

columns.title: Elapsed
columns.header_tooltip: Wall-clock time from run start to completion. A dash means the run has not concluded.

columns.title: vs usual
columns.header_tooltip: This run's elapsed over the median of the other successful runs of the same workflow and trigger loaded on this page. ▲ slower than usual, ▼ faster than usual, plain = within the usual range, – = not enough history (see n).

columns.title: n
columns.header_tooltip: How many comparable runs — same workflow and trigger, successful — are loaded on this page to form the baseline. Grey below 3: too few to call anything unusual.

columns.title: Started
columns.header_tooltip: When the run started, in your local time. Hover for UTC.

columns.title: Completed
columns.header_tooltip: When the run completed, in your local time. Hover for UTC.

columns.title: History
columns.header_tooltip: This workflow's runs on this page as a strip: one bar per run at its actual start time; bar height is elapsed relative to the workflow's longest; red = failed, dark = this run, dashed line = the median. Opens the workflow page.
